title: Cruise Control Accelerate Signal
plain: The computer is seeing an incorrect signal from the cruise control "Accel" button.
symptoms: Cruise control not working or cutting out

causes.name: Faulty cruise control switch on the steering wheel or stalk
Worn clockspring (the coiled wiring inside the steering wheel)

checks: Check whether the horn and other steering wheel buttons work
Watch the cruise switch signals on a scan tool while pressing each button
fix: Usually a new cruise control switch or clockspring.

title: Brake Switch "A" Circuit
plain: The computer sees a problem with the brake pedal switch signal. This switch turns on the brake lights and tells the car's computers when you're braking.
symptoms: Brake lights not working or staying on
Shifter may not come out of Park

causes.name: Misadjusted brake light switch or broken pedal stopper pad
Burned-out brake light bulbs (on some vehicles)
Wiring or connector problem at the switch

checks: Have someone confirm the brake lights work when the pedal is pressed
Check the stop lamp fuse and bulbs
Look at the brake switch signal on a scan tool while pressing the pedal
fix: Most often a new brake light switch, adjusted correctly.

title: Brake Switch "A" Circuit Low
plain: The brake pedal switch signal is stuck low, so the computer may not know when the brakes are applied.
symptoms: Brake lights not working or staying on
Shifter may not come out of Park
checks: Check the stop lamp fuse and that brake lights work
Check the switch signal on a scan tool while pressing the pedal
fix: Usually a new brake light switch or a fuse and wiring repair.

title: Brake Switch "A" Circuit High
plain: The brake pedal switch signal is stuck high, so the computer may think the brakes are always applied.
symptoms: Brake lights not working or staying on
Shifter may not come out of Park

causes.name: Faulty or stuck brake light switch
Misadjusted switch or broken pedal stopper pad

checks: Check whether the brake lights stay on with the pedal released
Look for a missing stopper pad on the brake pedal arm
fix: Usually a new brake light switch or adjustment.

title: Cruise Control System - Vehicle Speed Too High
plain: Cruise control shut itself off because the vehicle went faster than the highest speed the system allows, often on a steep downhill.

causes.name: Vehicle sped up past the cruise limit on a downhill
Faulty or erratic vehicle speed signal

checks: Note whether it happened going downhill
Check for vehicle or wheel speed sensor codes
fix: Often no repair is needed; clear the code. If it returns, check the speed sensor signal.

title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the cruise control vacuum solenoid. This part lets engine vacuum into the cruise servo on older vacuum-operated cruise systems.

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the cruise control vacuum solenoid wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the cruise control vacuum solenoid with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new cruise control vacuum solenoid if it tests bad.

title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit Low

Check related fuses and relays

fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new cruise control vacuum solenoid if it tests bad.

title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the thermostat heater. This part warms an electronic thermostat so the computer can open it early and keep the engine cooler under load.
symptoms: Engine may run hotter than normal under load
Temperature gauge may read higher than usual

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the thermostat heater wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the thermostat heater with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new thermostat assembly, since the heater is built into it.
